title: Pajson Agro India Ltd - 544657 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: H1 FY27 total income rose 23% YoY to about INR 145 crore, with EBITDA of about INR 20 crore (14% margin) and PAT of about INR 12.6 crore.
summary.overview: Pajson Agro reported H1 FY27 total income of about INR 145 crore (up 23% YoY), EBITDA of about INR 20 crore at a 14% margin, and PAT of about INR 12.6 crore. Plant utilisation rose to about 95% from 86% in FY26, with management saying demand is now ahead of capacity. The board approved a share-swap acquisition of 100% of Pacific Global FZCO, which runs a 60,000 MT cashew processing facility in Cote d'Ivoire, while the 35,000 MT Vizianagaram plant has slipped about 45 days after cyclones and is now expected to start trials by February. Margin compression versus last year was attributed to forex, freight and sourcing cost pressure.

up 190 bps vs H2 FY26 (as stated)
PAT up 19% vs H2 FY26 (as stated)

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from operations (H1 FY27, per analyst)

financial_highlights.value: about INR 170 per kg of raw cashew nut

segments.name: India processing (Andhra Pradesh, Visakhapatnam)
segments.commentary: Running close to full capacity at about 95% utilisation in H1 FY27 against 18,000 MT live capacity. H1 margin reported to have compressed from about 18% to 12-13% per analyst's read, which management attributed to forex, freight and shipping surcharges.

segments.name: Royal Meva (consumer brand)
segments.commentary: Contributed 4.6% of H1 FY27 revenue versus 1.36% in H1 FY26. Management targets 15% of total revenue in three to five years, growing slowly to protect margins.

segments.name: Pacific Global FZCO (Cote d'Ivoire, proposed acquisition)
segments.commentary: 60,000 MT facility, recently started production and described as pre-revenue for the company. Management expects about 50% utilisation in FY27 and full utilisation by FY28; realisation about 15% lower per kg than India, and margins higher than India, per management.

guidance_outlook: Vizianagaram (35,000 MT) trials now expected by February 2027 after roughly 45 days lost to three cyclones; commercial production targeted around Q4 FY27, with very little revenue from it in FY27.
Post-Vizianagaram, India capacity to be 53,000 MT; combined capacity 113,000 MT post Pacific Global acquisition.
Greenfield utilisation expected at 60-70% in FY28 with the current plant at near 90%; combined utilisation of 85-90% targeted for FY29.
Pacific Global consolidation expected in two to three months, with management saying it could occur in FY27 (around Jan-Mar 2027).

Management said working capital requirements will rise and that new working capital lines from financial institutions are expected as utilisation reaches 85-90%; no equity fundraise planned as of now.
Long-term aim of 5-8% global cashew market share within five to seven years; management declined to comment on FY28 EBITDA or top-line numbers.
capex_capacity: Vizianagaram greenfield plant: 35,000 MT, delayed by about two months due to three cyclones (Arnab, Musaru) that halted site work; trials targeted by February 2027; IPO proceeds being deployed as planned.

Acquisition of 100% of Pacific Global FZCO (60,000 MT Cote d'Ivoire plant) via preferential share issue at a valuation close to NAV, subject to shareholder and other approvals; consideration entirely in Pajson shares.

Pacific Global's Cote d'Ivoire plant was a greenfield project that the group took over roughly nine months to one year into construction; government tax holidays and subsidised rates expected over about a decade.
demand_pricing: Demand for kernels described as healthy; management says demand is now ahead of current capacity.
Institutional customers (food and snack confectionery) rose to 37.5% of revenue; 178 distributors across more than 20 states.
Raw cashew nut input costs were high; company chose to pass on prices gradually and built higher raw nut inventory, adding to working capital and interest costs.
H1 margin pressure attributed to forex, freight and shipping surcharges, and a stronger festive-season base in H1 FY26.
Management said Africa processing margins are about 5-7% higher than India, while acknowledging a 15% realisation gap for Pacific Global volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Pacific Global acquisition being consolidated, and how is it structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Pulkit Jain said it is a pure share swap with no cash to promoters; preferential shares equal to 100% of Pacific Global's value are issued to its existing shareholders, at a valuation close to NAV, with the share price set per SEBI rules.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 60,000 MT Pacific Global plant utilised and what is its valuation logic?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is expected to be about 50% in FY27 and full utilisation by FY28. Management said the entity is pre-revenue, having started operations only a few months earlier, so valuation is not based on profitable numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is expected from the Pacific Global realisation and consolidated margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation is about 15% lower per kg than India (current India H1 realisation about INR 170/kg RCN); Pulkit Jain said Africa margins are higher than India, with margin benefit from farm-gate sourcing expected in the long term rather than FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India margins compress in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Aayush Jain cited forex movement, freight and shipping surcharges that rose mid-season, and a stronger H1 FY26 base due to earlier festivities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and delay of the Vizianagaram plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Aayush Jain said three cyclones delayed the project by about 45 days, with trials now targeted for February and very little revenue from the new plant in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital and debt expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital needs will rise and debt will increase with volumes; Pacific Global has no long-term debt; Cote d'Ivoire lending rates are near India levels, while Nigerian working capital lines are 20-24%.

risks_watch: Promoter-led share swap with Pacific Global: related-party and minority protection concerns raised by several analysts; EPS accretion claimed but not quantified.
Vizianagaram commissioning slippage (trials now February 2027) and ramp-up to 60-70% utilisation in FY28.
Forex, freight and shipping surcharge pressure on India margins; management flagged geopolitical and currency risks as unprecedented.
Rising working capital and debt needs as utilisation scales; new working capital lines from institutions not yet secured.

Ability to fill the 60,000 MT Pacific Global plant, given the cashew market grows about 9-10% CAGR and India (about 30-35% of global demand) is the main consumption market; India import duty noted by an analyst.
Completion of the acquisition is subject to shareholder and other approvals; watch timing (management says two to three months).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, utilisation and long-term strategy, but cautious and evasive on numbers: management declined to quantify FY28 EBITDA or revenue at full utilisation and repeatedly stressed governance. Candour on delays (cyclones) and margin pressure was clear.
key_quotes: Our plant in Andhra Pradesh ran close to full capacity, and work on our new Vizianagaram facility is going as per plan.
So it is a total share swap deal without any cash consideration to the promoters of Pacific Global or the current Pajson Agro promoters.
We would rather forego a transaction than pursue one that cannot be demonstrated to be fair.
